receipts.summary: Source build identifiers were recorded in the private lab. No game files or private paths are published.
Primary community repositories and official native build documentation were reviewed.
A private UE 5.7 recovery host with Game, Editor, Client and Server targets was staged. It contains no recovered gameplay implementation.
Private Windows and Mac build scripts passed grouped syntax/preflight checks. Unreal compilation was not run.
Offline WdExtract build succeeded against pinned CUE4Parse commit 0415fe26eeba66ac0d814c2547b098219682066f. This is an extraction tool build, not a game build.

Six recovery/analysis tools were staged with source/version/hash receipts. Reflection was staged into the private recovery host and enabled for Editor only. Mirror managed publish and Ghidra launcher checks succeeded; no game import or Unreal compilation was performed.

Versioned source inventory records 308 files, 48,905,452,140 bytes, 75 PAK containers and 17 IoStore TOCs, including 15 encrypted TOCs and 150,663 chunk entries. Chunk entries are not asset counts. The isolated source copy matches all 308 file sizes and 98 selected executable/index hashes; UCAS bulk SHA-256 verification was not performed.

Parsed 6,864 public community JSON files into a private recovery catalog: 337,088,261 bytes and 18,659 exports, with 1,175 files containing Blueprint-generated classes. These are public community exports, not fresh decoding of the owned source build.

A keyless probe copied two optional texture bulk payloads from the source, each 33,554,432 bytes, using decoder 2.9.16. These are raw bulk payloads, not reconstructed textures, geometry or playable assets.

A private input-discovery utility passed synthetic positive and negative fixtures. A published archive-key candidate was rejected by normal mounting of this source build; no matching key was recovered and current-build mappings remain unresolved.
75 .pak filenames classified as 17 Unreal archives and 58 Chromium resource packs.
54 unique supplied candidates rejected by both validators on two encrypted PAK indices; no key values published.
No consistent forward AES-256 expanded-key schedules found in the stated initialized-section scope; this is not key absence proof.
Clear crash-reporter index mounted successfully; no gameplay assets recovered.
Visible mapping/relocation/delegation path recorded in private Ghidra evidence; no native game source recovered.
Selected launcher session/service boundary traced without starting a service or session.
Two routines confirmed to contain AES instructions; caller key provenance and archive relation unresolved.
Seven selected file/Ghidra regions matched; decompiler presentation and raw control flow were reconciled.
Completed the bounded state-processor trace and a byte-correlated focal decompile. Selected constants are proved; indirect target remains unresolved.
Ten matching section layouts plus PE metadata support common protected/restored layout, not decoded-code equality or crypto semantics.
Embedded MSI and service/control programs extracted as data; modular session boundaries recorded, no installation or key recovery.
Finite terminal SSA slice exported and correlated with the exact copied code range.
Saved-frame loads, context-pointer reload and return-site storage verified without inventing uninitialized values.
Exact base-relative XOR tail identity checked against versioned SSA and raw spill/alias evidence.
All 36 rounds of the operand hash chain certified, with effective image base kept symbolic.
Both eight-round table index calculations and their guarded control roles verified within the stated initialization scope.
Hash, indices, initial table data, raw pre-read write audit and executable range compose into a selected transfer; no live-memory claim.
Selected code range byte-correlated and decompiled; three proved branch outcomes produce an acyclic synthetic view, discarded after analysis.
